es: Formar paralelismo, tricolon y antítesis con la misma estructura gramatical en cada parte, cuidar la simetría del ritmo y repasar el énfasis con so y such.

teaching.en: The speaker uses parallelism when every part of the sentence has the same grammar: we want to learn, to share and to grow.
teaching.es: El orador usa el paralelismo cuando cada parte de la frase tiene la misma gramática: queremos aprender, compartir y crecer.
teaching.explanationEs: Paralelismo: cada parte repite la misma forma (aquí, to + verbo).
segments: The speaker uses parallelism when every part of the sentence has the
same grammar: we want to learn, to share and to grow.
teaching.audioText: The speaker uses parallelism when every part of the sentence has the same grammar: we want to learn, to share and to grow.

teaching.en: A tricolon gives a sentence the rhythm of three, as in safe streets, clean air and happy people, and the third part usually lands with the most weight.
teaching.es: Un tricolon da a la frase el ritmo de tres, como en calles seguras, aire limpio y gente feliz, y la tercera parte suele caer con más peso.
teaching.explanationEs: Tricolon: tres partes seguidas con la misma forma; la última cierra con fuerza.
segments: A tricolon gives a sentence the rhythm of three, as in safe streets, clean
air and happy people, and the third part usually lands with the most weight.
teaching.audioText: A tricolon gives a sentence the rhythm of three, as in safe streets, clean air and happy people, and the third part usually lands with the most weight.

teaching.en: Antithesis places opposite ideas in the same structure, such as young in years but old in wisdom, so the contrast feels balanced and complete.
teaching.es: La antítesis coloca ideas opuestas en la misma estructura, como joven en años pero viejo en sabiduría, y así el contraste resulta equilibrado y completo.
teaching.explanationEs: Antítesis: opuestos (young/old) con estructura igual (adjetivo + in + nombre).
segments: Antithesis places opposite ideas in the same structure, such as young in
years but old in wisdom, so the contrast feels balanced and complete.
teaching.audioText: Antithesis places opposite ideas in the same structure, such as young in years but old in wisdom, so the contrast feels balanced and complete.

teaching.en: If one part changes its grammar, the symmetry breaks and the balance of the whole sentence is lost, so keep every part in the same form.
teaching.es: Si una parte cambia de gramática, la simetría se rompe y se pierde el equilibrio de toda la frase, así que mantén cada parte con la misma forma.
teaching.explanationEs: Simetría y equilibrio dependen de que las partes suenen igual.
segments: If one part changes its grammar, the symmetry breaks and the balance of
the whole sentence is lost, so keep every part in the same form.
teaching.audioText: If one part changes its grammar, the symmetry breaks and the balance of the whole sentence is lost, so keep every part in the same form.

teaching.en: An eloquent speaker often lets the final part grow longer or stronger, which helps to hammer home the main point.
teaching.es: Un orador elocuente suele dejar que la parte final sea más larga o más fuerte, lo que ayuda a machacar la idea principal.
teaching.explanationEs: Hammer home = dejar clara una idea a base de insistencia rítmica.
segments: An eloquent speaker often lets the final part grow longer
or stronger, which helps to hammer home the main point.
teaching.audioText: An eloquent speaker often lets the final part grow longer or stronger, which helps to hammer home the main point.

teaching.en: It was such a clear structure, and the speaker was so calm, that the speech felt persuasive and memorable in equal measure.
teaching.es: Era una estructura tan clara, y el orador estaba tan tranquilo, que el discurso resultó persuasivo y fácil de recordar en la misma medida.
teaching.explanationEs: Repaso: such + a + adjetivo + nombre + that; so + adjetivo + that.
segments: It was such a clear structure, and the speaker was so
calm, that the speech felt persuasive and memorable in equal measure.
teaching.audioText: It was such a clear structure, and the speaker was so calm, that the speech felt persuasive and memorable in equal measure.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con paralelismo: «Queremos aprender, compartir y crecer.»

choices.text: We want to learn, sharing and to grow.
We want to learn, to share and to grow.
We want learning, to share and growing.

feedback.es: Las tres partes usan to + verbo: esa igualdad de forma crea el paralelismo.

hint.es: Las tres partes deben tener la misma forma.

origin.text: A student drafts a line for the school council: she wants three verbs, each built in exactly the same way, to close her opening paragraph.

prompt.es: Completa la antítesis: «Es fácil empezar, pero difícil terminar.»

feedback.es: Hard (o difficult) se opone a easy y mantiene la estructura adjetivo + to + verbo.

origin.text: Her slogan is a perfect antithesis: it is easy to start, but ___ to finish. The opposite adjective keeps the same structure as the first part.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Queremos una escuela que escuche, aprenda y dirija.»

answer.text: We want a school that listens, learns and leads

feedback.es: Tricolon: tres verbos en tercera persona con la misma forma (-s).

hint.es: Tres verbos seguidos con la misma terminación.

prompt.es: Une en un tricolon: limpiar, plantar y pintar.

answer.text: We clean the park, plant trees and paint the benches.
accepted: We clean the park, plant trees and paint the benches.
We clean the park, we plant trees and we paint benches.
We clean the park, plant the trees and paint the benches.

feedback.es: El tricolon une tres acciones con la misma forma; and introduce la última.

origin.text: We clean the park. We plant trees. We paint the benches.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su técnica.

pairs: We listen, we learn, we lead.
Reading opens minds; writing opens doors.
It was such a clear plan that nobody argued.

feedback.es: Opuestos con la misma forma son antítesis; tres verbos seguidos son tricolon; dos partes iguales son paralelismo; such a + nombre da énfasis.

pairs: We listen, we learn, we lead.
Reading opens minds; writing opens doors.
It was such a clear plan that nobody argued.

prompt.es: Elige cómo unir las dos frases con énfasis: «La voz era tan fuerte que todos escucharon.»

choices.text: The voice was such strong that everyone listened.
The voice was so a strong voice that everyone listened.
The voice was so strong that everyone listened.

feedback.es: Con un adjetivo solo se usa so + adjetivo + that; such exige un nombre: such a strong voice.

origin.text: At the school assembly, the speaker talked about litter for ten minutes. Her voice was strong, and nobody looked at their phones.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué contraste construye la oradora sobre los alumnos.

choices.text: A lot of talent but little time.
A lot of time but little talent.
A lot of rooms but few teachers.

feedback.es: Dice que los alumnos son ricos en talento pero pobres en tiempo: la antítesis rich in talent, poor in time.

origin.audio: Friends, this school has given us so much: it has taught us to think, to question and to care. Yet it has asked for so little in return. We are rich in talent, but poor in time; ready in spirit, but tired in body. Today I am not asking for something impossible. I am asking for one hour, one classroom and one chance to make our voices heard.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige con qué propósito pide solo «una hora».

choices.text: To admit that the students are not serious.
To make the request sound small and easy to accept.
To warn the school that the students will go on strike.

feedback.es: Tras decir que no pide algo imposible, enumera una hora, un aula y una oportunidad: presenta la petición como pequeña para que sea fácil aceptarla.

origin.audio: Friends, this school has given us so much: it has taught us to think, to question and to care. Yet it has asked for so little in return. We are rich in talent, but poor in time; ready in spirit, but tired in body. Today I am not asking for something impossible. I am asking for one hour, one classroom and one chance to make our voices heard.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pequeño en tamaño, grande en corazón.»

feedback.es: Big se opone a small y mantiene la estructura adjetivo + in + nombre: así se cierra la antítesis.

origin.text: Her speech ends with a pair of opposites: small in size, ___ in heart. The two parts share the same structure, which gives the ending its symmetry.

prompt.es: Reescribe con antítesis: «Hoy discutimos, mañana actuaremos.»

answer.text: We argue today, but we will act tomorrow.
accepted: We argue today, but we will act tomorrow.
Today we argue, but tomorrow we will act.
We argue today but will act tomorrow.
Today we argue, yet tomorrow we act.

feedback.es: Se enfrentan today y tomorrow con la misma estructura, unidas por but.

origin.text: We argue today. We will act tomorrow.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que mantiene el paralelismo que subraya la profesora.

choices.text: She loves reading, to write and painting.
She loves to read, writing and paint.
She loves reading, writing and painting.

feedback.es: Las tres actividades están en -ing: sin mezclar formas, el paralelismo se conserva.

origin.text: Reviewing a draft, a teacher underlines one sentence and writes beside it: the three activities must share exactly the same form.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue un discurso tan claro que todos lo recordaron durante semanas.»

feedback.es: Delante de a + adjetivo + nombre se usa such, no so.

origin.text: The speaker chose every word with care. It was ___ a clear speech that everybody remembered it for weeks.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué postura adopta la oradora ante el pasado.

choices.text: She admits it was hard but wants to move on.
She denies that there were any problems.
She blames the audience for the old arguments.

feedback.es: No niega el pasado, pero pide mirar más allá: reconoce la dificultad y propone avanzar.

origin.audio: Yesterday was difficult, but tomorrow will be brighter. Yesterday we were divided; tomorrow we will stand together. The speaker does not deny the past, yet she asks her audience to look beyond it.
